How is the rent relief calculated for personal income tax?
Rent relief is 20% of the annual rent you paid, capped at NGN 500,000, so you get whichever is lower. Claim it in your annual return and declare the actual rent paid.
Someone told me I can deduct my full annual rent with no cap. Is that right?
No, that is not right. The relief is 20% of the annual rent paid, subject to a maximum of NGN 500,000 - whichever is lower. It is not a deduction of the full rent.
Are school fees an eligible deduction for personal income tax?
No - school fees are not an eligible deduction under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. They are not on the section 30(2)(a) list, so they cannot reduce your chargeable income.
Someone told me school fees can be deducted from taxable income. Is that right?

No, that is not correct. School fees are not deductible: the eligible deductions in section 30(2)(a) of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 do not include school fees, so they do not reduce your chargeable income.
I'm planning my budget for the children's education. Can school fees be claimed as a tax deduction?
No - school fees are not deductible. The section 30(2)(a) list of eligible deductions under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 does not include school fees, so they cannot reduce your chargeable income.
Can I deduct school fees, and what does the exact legal provision say?

No - school fees are not deductible. The eligible deductions are listed in section 30(2)(a) of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, covering NHF, NHIS, Pension Reform Act contributions, mortgage interest, life insurance or annuity premiums and rent relief; school fees are not among them.
Pension contributions and NHF contributions both reduce tax - so what actually separates them?

Both reduce your chargeable income as eligible deductions, but they are separate schemes. Pension contributions are made under the Pension Reform Act, while NHF contributions go to the National Housing Fund. Pension is the contributory retirement scheme; NHF is a housing fund contribution, and each is claimed separately.
Someone told me pension and NHF contributions are the same thing for tax. Is that right?

No, they are not the same. Pension contributions are made under the Pension Reform Act and NHF contributions go to the National Housing Fund; both are eligible deductions that reduce chargeable income, but they are separate schemes claimed separately.
I'm checking my payslip deductions. How do pension and NHF contributions differ for tax?

They are separate eligible deductions. Pension contributions under the Pension Reform Act and NHF contributions both reduce your chargeable income, but pension is the contributory retirement scheme while NHF is a housing fund contribution.
What is the difference between pension and NHF contributions for tax? Please cite the exact legal provision.

Under section 30(2)(a) of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, NHF contributions are deductible under item (i) and Pension Reform Act contributions under item (iii). Both reduce your chargeable income, but they are separate schemes: pension is the contributory retirement scheme and NHF is a housing fund contribution.
Do tax rules differ between Abuja and Lagos?

No. The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 applies throughout Nigeria, so the rules and rates are the same in Abuja and Lagos. Only the tax authority that handles your tax differs - LIRS in Lagos, the FCT Internal Revenue Service in Abuja.
Someone told me the tax rules are different in Abuja and Lagos. Is that right?

No, that is not right. The same Nigeria Tax Act 2025 rules apply throughout Nigeria, so the bands and reliefs do not change. What changes is the tax authority: LIRS in Lagos and the FCT Internal Revenue Service in Abuja.
I may relocate from Lagos to Abuja next year. Will the tax rules change for me?
No. The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 applies throughout Nigeria, so the rules stay the same; only the tax authority you deal with changes - LIRS in Lagos and the FCT Internal Revenue Service in Abuja.
Do tax rules differ between Abuja and Lagos? Please cite the exact legal provision.
No. Section 2 of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 provides that the Act applies throughout Nigeria, so the same rules apply in Abuja and Lagos; only the relevant tax authority differs.
If someone has no income at all, do they still need to file a tax return?
No. With no income you have no tax to pay and no annual return is required of you. The annual return duty applies to taxable persons - employees and people with taxable income.
Someone told me I still have to file tax as a student even with no income. Is that right?
No. With no income there is nothing to assess and no annual return is required; the annual return obligation applies to taxable persons, not to a student with no income.
I'm a full-time university student and I earn nothing. Do I need to file tax?
No. With no income you have no tax liability and no annual return is required of you; the filing duty applies to taxable persons and employees.
I'm a student with no income - do I need to file? Please cite the exact legal provision.
No. Section 13(1) of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 requires an annual return from every taxable person; a student with no income is not taxable, so no annual return is required of you.
What are the 2026 income tax bands and rates?

The 2026 bands: the first NGN 800,000 at 0%; the next NGN 2,200,000 at 15%; the next NGN 9,000,000 at 18%; the next NGN 13,000,000 at 21%; the next NGN 25,000,000 at 23%; and anything above NGN 50,000,000 at 25%.
Someone told me the top rate is 30% and the first band is 5%. Is that right?

No. The 2026 bands are: the first NGN 800,000 at 0%; the next NGN 2,200,000 at 15%; the next NGN 9,000,000 at 18%; the next NGN 13,000,000 at 21%; the next NGN 25,000,000 at 23%; and anything above NGN 50,000,000 at 25%.
What is the PAYE remittance deadline?
PAYE deducted from salaries is remitted to the state tax authority by the 10th day of the month following the month of deduction.
Someone told me PAYE is remitted by the 21st of the following month rather than the 10th. Is that right?
No, that is not right. PAYE deducted from salaries is remitted to the relevant state internal revenue service by the 10th day of the month following the month in which it was deducted.
How is overpaid tax refunded?

Overpaid tax is refunded after an audit by the relevant tax authority. The refund is paid within 90 days of the authority's decision, with the option of a set-off against tax liability, and the claim must be made in writing within six years after the end of the year of assessment.
Someone told me you must claim a refund within 90 days and the authority then pays it within six years. Is that right?
No, that is the wrong way round. The written refund claim must be made within six years after the end of the year of assessment, and the refund is paid within 90 days of the tax authority's decision.
What are the limits on voluntary pension contributions, and how are they made?

Voluntary pension contributions go through your employer into your retirement savings account. You notify your employer in writing of your intention and the amount; a contribution cannot exceed one-third of the month's salary and can be made only once a month.
Someone told me I can pay voluntary pension contributions straight to the pension administrator, with no limit. Is that right?

No. Voluntary contributions must go through your employer into your RSA, and you must notify your employer in writing of the intention and the amount. A contribution cannot exceed one-third of the month's salary and can be made only once a month.
What evidence does a deduction claim need?

The deduction must be claimed in writing in the prescribed form, and the relevant tax authority may require documentary evidence in support. Without adequate evidence, the authority may refuse or reduce the deduction.
Someone told me I can claim a deduction without putting anything in writing or showing proof. Is that right?

No. A deduction is not allowed unless it is claimed in writing in the prescribed form, and the tax authority may require documentary evidence; if the evidence is absent or inadequate, it may refuse or reduce the deduction.
Wetin be the rent relief rule?
Rent relief na 20% of the annual rent wey you pay, but e no fit pass NGN 500,000 - whichever one lower na im you go use. You must declare the actual rent, and dem fit ask you for evidence.
Abeg, school fees dey count as deduction for tax?

No. School fees are not deductible. You no fit remove school fees from your chargeable income - dem no dey among the eligible deductions under the tax law. The deductions wey dey allowed na NHF, NHIS, Pension Reform Act contributions, mortgage interest, life insurance or annuity premium, and rent relief.
Pension and NHF money - wetin be the difference when dem dey calculate tax?

Both pension contribution under the Pension Reform Act and NHF contribution na eligible deductions - dem dey reduce your chargeable income before tax. The main difference na the obligation: pension contribution na mandatory for covered employees, so your employer dey deduct am from your salary and remit am. NHF contribution na mandatory for public-sector workers, but for private-sector workers e dey voluntary. So pension dey compulsory for covered employees, while NHF fit be voluntary depending on where you work.
Abeg, tax rules dey different between Abuja and Lagos?

No, the tax rules no different. The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 dey apply throughout Nigeria, so the same bands and deductions dey for Abuja and Lagos. Wetin dey different na the tax authority wey dey administer the tax: PAYE dey go the state internal revenue service - LIRS for Lagos, FCT Internal Revenue Service for Abuja.
My salary na NGN 1,620,000 a year and I dey pay rent of NGN 350,000 a year. How much tax I go pay?

Gross income: NGN 1,620,000. Relief wey dey apply: rent NGN 70,000 (20% of rent paid) - total relief NGN 70,000. Chargeable income: NGN 1,550,000. Band breakdown: first NGN 800,000 at 0% = NGN 0; next NGN 750,000 at 15% = NGN 112,500. Total tax: NGN 112,500.
